# `delete_image`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Delete image files (and their accessory files) by name from the image folder or a chosen storage.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe5210, AddImages @0xae600, DeleteMedia @0x12da60, remove_file @0x1242f0 (64-bit build) |

Params carry a required name (a string or an array of strings) and, in the object form, an optional storage. Names are appended directly to the image directory path with no length, component, extension or traversal check seen. Directories are enumerated for media and logs, default folders are skipped and removal is tried unless the directory is a default one. A recording AVI/MP4 gives 206; ENOENT and ENOTEMPTY count as removed. After each successful deletion the favourites database entry is removed and the free-space checker refreshed. The first failing deletion stops the call and earlier deletions stay. Access, log and default-folder skips alone are not errors. An empty array or one with no strings returns success without deleting. Non-string array items are skipped silently. The call is synchronous and can block on the filesystem or database. The positional form is [name] or [[name1, name2]]; a bare scalar string params is not accepted and gives 100.

Side effects: Permanently deletes files and possibly directories from device storage, removes favourites database entries and refreshes the free-space checker. No rollback, no timeout, no camera or mount-state precondition.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"delete_image"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array | yes | - | Object form {name, storage?}, or positional [name] / [[name1, name2]] (storage is not available positionally). A bare string is not accepted. [READ] |
| `params.name` | string\|array | no | - | File name, or array of names, relative to the image directory. Non-string array items are skipped; an empty array is a no-op success. No default. [READ] |
| `params.storage` | string | no | the current image save path | Storage selector, matched case-insensitively against the model-dependent storage names (sd, udisk, plus emmc on models that have it). A missing or non-string value silently uses the current image path. An unrecognised string gives 204. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | name missing, null or of the wrong container type (also the dispatcher case: method missing or not a string) | `invalid request` |
| 204 | storage string not recognised | `out of limit` |
| 206 | Target is an AVI/MP4 currently being recorded | `capture is active` |
| 207 | Other deletion failure with no code set (thread-local code otherwise forwarded) | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |

Codes other than 100, 204 and 206 originate below the inspected layer and are unresolved.

## Example

Request, two-files - Object form (names invented):

```json
{"id":171,"method":"delete_image","params":{"name":["M31_stack_20260131.fit","M31_stack_20260131.jpg"]}}
```

Request, one-file-storage:

```json
{"id":172,"method":"delete_image","params":{"name":"old_frame.fit","storage":"sd"}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"delete_image","result":0,"code":0,"id":171}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"delete_image","error":"out of limit","code":204,"id":173}
```
